dynamic.title: Dynamic tariff
dynamic.description: How does Home Assistant know your dynamic tariff's price? Recommended: exchange price plus surcharges – only then can Tarifwacht also calculate the time before the setup (looking back, importing statistics).

menu_options.dynamic_total: Sensor with the total price (also your own tariff) – from the setup on only

dynamic_market.title: Dynamic tariff: exchange price plus surcharges
dynamic_market.description: Price per kWh = (exchange price + grid fee + taxes and levies + supplier surcharge) × (1 + VAT). Enter the surcharges net, i.e. without VAT – Tarifwacht adds it itself. If the price sheet only shows a gross value, divide it by 1.19 (at 19 %).

data_description.price_entity: Day-ahead price in €/kWh without VAT, ideally with a forecast: the market price of the EPEX Spot integration, or (experimental) Nord Pool or ENTSO-E from HACS, each without VAT and surcharges.
data_description.grid_fee: Energy-related grid fee of your grid operator, net (without VAT), from its price sheet.
data_description.levies: Electricity tax, concession fee and levies added up, net (without VAT).
data_description.margin: What the supplier adds per kWh, net (without VAT). With EPEX Spot: its absolute surcharge in cent (0.15 €/kWh = 15 ct); then leave grid fee and taxes empty.
data_description.base_price: Optional, incl. VAT. Booked pro rata per day.

details_section.name: More (optional)
details_section.description: VAT (19 % unless your contract says otherwise).

dynamic_total.title: Dynamic tariff: total price sensor
dynamic_total.description: A sensor that already contains the whole price per kWh – the total price of a dynamic tariff (exchange price plus grid fee, levies, taxes, supplier surcharge and VAT) or your own tariff as a template sensor in €/kWh. A sensor only knows its own past: calculates only from the setup on (no lookback, no import of statistics) – for a dynamic tariff better choose “exchange price plus surcharges”.

data_description.price_entity: In €/kWh, ideally with a price forecast per quarter hour or hour: the total price of the EPEX Spot integration, (experimental) Nord Pool or ENTSO-E from HACS, or any other sensor in €/kWh, e.g. a template with your own tariff.
data_description.base_price: Optional, incl. VAT. Booked pro rata per day.

modul3_fixed.title: Modul 3 ({tariff})
modul3_fixed.description: With a controllable consumer (heat pump, wallbox) under § 14a EnWG Modul 3 the grid fee depends on the time of day. If your fixed-price supplier passes it on, the energy price stays fixed and only its grid fee part changes: in the low-load (NT) and high-load (HT) windows of the chosen quarters the price is the fixed price + (grid fee of the window − grid fee contained) × (1 + VAT), otherwise the fixed price ({price} ct/kWh). Applies to the meter's whole grid purchase. Values from the start of the tariff; enter a new price sheet as a price change.

user.title: PV and battery
user.description:
What PV and battery saved under each tariff: compared with buying all consumption from the grid. Computed every hour from the long-term statistics of the meters.

Tip: if you also use [Einspeisewacht]({einspeisewacht_url}) or [Speicherwacht]({speicherwacht_url}), these fields are filled in already.

data_description.feed_in_entity: Energy fed into the grid (kWh counter), e.g. of the smart meter.
data_description.pv_entity: PV energy (kWh counter). With a battery on the same inverter (hybrid inverter): its AC output.
data_description.charged_entity: Optional, together with “Battery discharged”: energy into the battery (kWh counter).
data_description.discharged_entity: Optional: energy out of the battery (kWh counter).
data_description.feed_in_rate: What you get per kWh fed in.
data_description.negative_unpaid: Section 51 EEG: plants commissioned from 25 February 2025 with a smart meter get nothing in quarter hours with a negative exchange price.

market_section.name: Exchange price for § 51 (optional)
market_section.description: Only needed for “No payment at negative prices” if there is no exchange price tariff.

data_description.market_entity: Day-ahead price in €/kWh (e.g. EPEX Spot), only for the rule above. Empty: the exchange price tariff's sensor.

purchase_section.name: Purchase (optional)
purchase_section.description: For “paid back”: what PV and battery cost and since when they run. Tarifwacht sets this against what they saved since that day.

data_description.pv_cost: Gross, in €, e.g. from the invoice (minus any subsidy). Empty: no payback.
data_description.pv_since: Day of commissioning. Savings before it do not count.
data_description.battery_cost: Gross, in €. Only with the battery meters.
data_description.battery_since: Empty: the same day as the PV. For a battery added later, its own day.

battery_same.title: Battery
battery_same.description: Your data suggest **yes**: the PV meter counts at night while the battery discharges.

data.same_inverter: Battery on the same inverter as the PV

data_description.same_inverter: Yes for a hybrid inverter (e.g. Fronius Gen24, Huawei, Kostal Plenticore): PV and battery share one inverter. No for a battery with its own inverter (e.g. SMA Sunny Boy Storage, Anker SOLIX, Zendure, Maxxisun).

battery_own.title: Battery
battery_own.description: Your data suggest **no**: the PV meter stays at zero at night while the battery discharges.

data.same_inverter: Battery on the same inverter as the PV

data_description.same_inverter: Yes for a hybrid inverter (e.g. Fronius Gen24, Huawei, Kostal Plenticore): PV and battery share one inverter. No for a battery with its own inverter (e.g. SMA Sunny Boy Storage, Anker SOLIX, Zendure, Maxxisun).

battery_unknown.title: Battery
battery_unknown.description: Your data do not tell yet (too few nights with the battery discharging).

data.same_inverter: Battery on the same inverter as the PV

data_description.same_inverter: Yes for a hybrid inverter (e.g. Fronius Gen24, Huawei, Kostal Plenticore): PV and battery share one inverter. No for a battery with its own inverter (e.g. SMA Sunny Boy Storage, Anker SOLIX, Zendure, Maxxisun).

compare.name: Compare tariffs
compare.description: Cost of every tariff of a meter in a period, the cheapest first, also per month. Before the setup estimated from the hourly long-term statistics; Tarifwacht loads the exchange prices of that time from SMARD.de.

start.name: Start
start.description: Optional. Without: since the setup. An earlier start uses the meter's hourly values from the long-term statistics.

import_statistics.name: Import statistics
import_statistics.description: Writes the hours before the sensors' first long-term statistics (energy, costs, difference, saving by PV and battery) so statistics cards and graphs also show the time before the setup. With “Replace existing statistics” the hours from the start on are recalculated with the current tariffs, too (after a tariff was corrected). Changes the statistics database – create a backup first.

config_entry.name: Meter
config_entry.description: The Tarifwacht entry whose sensors get the history.

start.name: Start
start.description: First day to import, before the setup (with “Replace existing statistics” also later). Not earlier than the meter's long-term statistics.

replace.name: Replace existing statistics
replace.description: Also recalculate the hours that already have statistics, from the start up to the last full hour, with the current tariffs. Without it only the time before the first statistics is filled in. The button “Recalculate statistics” on the meter's device does the same from the first statistics on.

start_after_end.message: The start must be before the end.

smard_failed.message: Exchange prices could not be loaded from SMARD.de ({error}). Please try again later.

import_start_after_setup.message: The start must be before the setup of this entry – after it, the sensors already have statistics.

import_no_statistics_yet.message: The sensors have no statistics yet. Home Assistant creates them every hour – please try again in an hour.

import_nothing_to_import.message: Nothing to import: the statistics already reach back to this day.

import_prices_missing.message: Nothing imported: every tariff lacks prices in this period. A tariff with a total price sensor has no prices from before the setup – add it as “exchange price plus surcharges” as well.

import_busy.message: The statistics of this entry are being imported or recalculated right now – please wait until that is done.

import_nothing_to_recalculate.message: Nothing to recalculate: Home Assistant has not compiled a full hour of these sensors since the start yet. Please try again in an hour.

recalculated.message: {name}: the long-term statistics of {count} sensors from {start} to {end} are recalculated with the current tariffs. Statistics graphs and the card show the new values; the sensors continue from them.

recalculated_skipped.message: Left out because prices are missing: {tariffs}.

recalculated_implausible.message: {count} hours with an implausible meter change were left out (first: {hours}).

price_unit.title: Price sensor with an unsupported unit ({name})
price_unit.description: The price sensor {entity} reports {unit}. Tarifwacht uses prices as they are and needs €/kWh, so it ignores this sensor's prices for now. Set the unit to €/kWh in the price integration, or choose another sensor for the tariff (Tarifwacht → tariff → Reconfigure). This message disappears once the sensor reports €/kWh.

meter_unit.title: Meter with an unsupported unit ({name})
meter_unit.description: The meter {entity} reports {unit}. Tarifwacht needs Wh, kWh or MWh and books nothing until then. Choose another meter (Tarifwacht → ⋮ → Reconfigure). This message disappears once the meter reports a supported unit.

missing_entity.title: Entity missing ({name})
missing_entity.description: {entities} no longer exists. Tarifwacht books nothing without the meter, and a tariff without its price sensor waits for its prices. Renamed entities are followed automatically; if one was deleted or replaced, choose another one: the meter under Tarifwacht → ⋮ → Reconfigure, a price sensor in the tariff (Tarifwacht → tariff → Reconfigure). This message disappears once the entity is back.

own_entity.title: Tarifwacht sensor chosen as a source ({name})
own_entity.description: {entities} belongs to Tarifwacht itself: the entry would read its own results. So Tarifwacht does not read it – without the meter the entry books no consumption, a tariff without its price sensor gets no prices. Figures already booked stay. Choose the real source: the meter under Tarifwacht → ⋮ → Reconfigure, a price sensor in the tariff (Tarifwacht → tariff → Reconfigure). This message disappears once no Tarifwacht sensor is chosen as a source.

late_prices.title: Prices missing ({name})
late_prices.description: For {tariffs}, the price of a past quarter hour is still missing. Day-ahead prices are normally known the day before, so the price sensor may have failed. Consumption waits for its price for 24 hours; after that it is counted without a price (never as free). This message disappears once the prices arrive.

backfill_failed.title: Consumption could not be read from the recorder ({name})
backfill_failed.description: After the update from 0.1.0b1, Tarifwacht reads the consumption since setup from the recorder once. This failed: {error}. Live booking is not affected; the next start of Home Assistant tries again.

statistics_outdated.title: Past statistics show old prices ({name})
statistics_outdated.description: A tariff (or PV and battery) of {name} was changed. Tarifwacht applies it to the whole period and the sensors already show the new totals – but the long-term statistics of past hours (statistics graphs, the months of the card, values per day) still hold the old ones. Press the button “Recalculate statistics” on the device {name} (Settings → Devices & services → Tarifwacht). Create a backup first. This notice disappears afterwards.
